pages.text: Mining and chopping run on your $(l:lemursaucepacket:skills)skills$(/l): better tools, harder ores and rarer trees each wait on a level. This page is the how-to: whole trees from one chop, finding ore, the ore veins that never run out, and the tools and machines that save you time.

pages.title: What your tools need
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)A level to use them.$() Pickaxes and shovels need Mining, axes need Woodcutting and hoes need Farming: stone tools at 5, golden at 10, iron at 15, diamond at 30, netherite at 50 ($(l:lemursaucepacket:skills)Skills$(/l)). A red "❣ Requires" line on the tooltip names the skill and the level; it turns green with a tick once you have it.

$(li)$(bold)Hardness for harder ores.$() A better pickaxe isn't enough here: harder blocks need a Hardness tome on the pickaxe and a Mining level. Iron, zinc and lapis take Hardness I (Mining 10), gold and redstone II (20), diamonds, emeralds and obsidian III (30), ancient debris IV (40). The tomes are on $(l:lemursaucepacket:enchanting)Enchanting$(/l).$(br)$(li)$(bold)Woodcutting for rarer trees.$() Oak, birch and spruce come down for anyone. Jungle trees need Woodcutting 15, cherry 50, redwoods 70; without the level the log won't break. Every tree's level is in $(l:lemursaucepacket:skills)Skills$(/l).

pages.title: Getting the XP
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Fresh ground only.$() Breaking a block you placed yourself pays no skill XP, so pulling up your own blocks and putting them back earns nothing. Train on what the world made.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Machines pay whoever is near.$() When a Create drill, saw or harvester does the work, every player within 16 blocks of it gets the Mining, Woodcutting or Farming, as if they'd done it by hand ($(l:lemursaucepacket:create-tips)Machine XP$(/l)). A cobblestone generator's blocks pay a machine a tenth. Tools that break many blocks at once (the Lumber Axe, the Excavator's Pickaxe, the Harvester's Scythe) pay too, for

every block.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Hold Shift$() over a block in your inventory: its tooltip lists the XP it pays to break. Iron ore pays 25 Mining, a log 12 Woodcutting.$(br)$(li)$(bold)No vein mining.$() Project MMO's vein miner is switched off.

pages.title: Felling trees
pages.text: The $(bold)Lumber Axe$() (Woodcutting 30; made in mechanical crafters, see $(l:lemursaucepacket:gear)Gear$(/l)) brings a whole tree down from one log. Every other axe chops one log at a time.$(br2)$(li)$(bold)Sneak$() to chop a single log.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Everything lands where you cut.$() The logs drop at the block you broke, and the leaves around the tree break at once, so saplings and apples fall too. Leaves you placed yourself stay.

$(li)$(bold)Durability.$() Felling costs about one point of durability for every four logs. A worn axe fells as many logs as it has durability for, then breaks: mend it before a big tree.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Giant trees don't fall.$() A tree of more than 200 logs is too big. A message above your hotbar says so, and you chop it log by log.$(br)$(li)$(bold)One kind of log at a time.$() Only logs of the kind you cut come down. Crimson and warped trees bring their wart blocks with them, mangroves their roots.

$(li)$(bold)Mind your builds.$() To the axe, logs with leaves beside the top one are a tree. Sneak when you take apart anything built of logs.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Turn it off$() for yourself with $(#e0ac46)/fallingtree toggle$(), and back on the same way.$(br)$(li)$(bold)A mechanical saw$() (Woodcutting 15 to make) fells a whole tree when it cuts the bottom log. On a moving contraption it cuts every tree it runs into. It works at the Woodcutting level of whoever placed it or last right-clicked it: a tree past that level stays standing.

pages.title: Finding ore
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Where an ore generates.$() Press $(bold)U$() over an ore in JEI (or $(bold)R$() over what it drops, like raw iron) and open the $(bold)World Generation$() tab. It shows the heights the ore generates at, the biomes (click for the full list), how big its clusters are and how many a chunk gets, and what it drops with Fortune or Silk Touch. It reads this server's real world generation.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Which tool a block takes.$() Look at a block: the block info at the top of your screen (Jade) shows the tool that harvests it. Hardness comes on top of that.

$(li)$(bold)Create's coloured stones.$() Crimsite, veridium, asurine and ochrum come in big striped bands underground, between about Y −30 and 70. They're stone, so any pickaxe takes them without Hardness, and crushing wheels turn them into crushed ore now and then:$(br2)$(#b9a98a)Stone - Each block crushes into$()$(br)$(bold)Veridium$() - Crushed copper 80 % of the time, and a copper nugget 80 %$(br)$(bold)Crimsite$() - Crushed iron 40 %, and an iron nugget 40 %$(br)$(bold)Asurine$() - Crushed zinc 30 %, and a zinc nugget 30 %$(br)$(bold)Ochrum$() - Crushed gold 20 %, and a gold nugget 20 %

$(li)$(bold)The Lost Candle$() (from Labyrinth chests; Mining 40 to use). Right-click a block with it: if coal, copper, iron, gold or diamond ore is within 8 blocks, it rings and names the ore. It works every 3 seconds.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Light as you go.$() A torch, lantern or other light in either hand lights the area around you. It's on your screen only: the real light level doesn't change, so monsters still spawn wherever you haven't placed torches. A torch held underwater goes dark.
$(li)$(bold)Desert temples$() give you Mining Fatigue while you're inside, until someone slays the temple's Pharaoh. Then the curse lifts for good.

pages.title: Ore veins that never run out
pages.text: Create Ore Excavation hides ore veins underground that never run out: find one with an $(bold)Ore Vein Finder$(), then drill it with a $(bold)Drilling Machine$(). A vein fills one chunk, and any number of machines can share it.$(br2)$(#b9a98a)Where - Veins$()$(br)$(bold)Overworld$() - Coal, copper, iron, gold, zinc, lapis, redstone, and water (for the Fluid Well Extractor)$(br)$(bold)Nether$() - Quartz, glowstone and gold nuggets

There are no diamond, emerald or netherite veins in this pack. Veins are rare: expect one of each kind in every 2,000 by 2,000 blocks or so, water veins four times as often and Nether gold a quarter as often.

pages.title: The Ore Vein Finder
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Right-click$() with it, anywhere. It reports a vein in the chunk you're in ("Found in Chunk"), in one next to it ("Found nearby"), or traces of one farther off, with a rough distance ("Found traces of: Raw Iron (~300 blocks away)"). Use it again as you walk: the distance tells you whether you're getting closer. It works every 5 seconds.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Making one$() takes Mining 35, an eye of ender, an amethyst shard, a redstone ore block and two sticks. Eyes of ender need Brewing 55 to craft, and a redstone ore block needs Silk Touch and Mining 20, so a team or a trade helps.

$(li)$(bold)The Ore Vein Atlas$() (Mining 35: a chest, an amethyst shard, a map and a book and quill) keeps a record of veins. Click a finished Sample Drill or a running Drilling Machine with it. In the atlas, set a target vein, or exclude and hide others; with the atlas in your inventory, the finder reports only your target.$(br)$(li)$(bold)A Sample Drill$() reads a vein you've found. Place it on the spot with a Copper Backtank (with air in it) on top, click it to start, and when it has finished one cycle, click it with the atlas.

pages.title: The Drilling Machine
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Build it$() in mechanical crafters (brass blocks and sheets, casings, a mechanical drill, precision mechanisms, sturdy sheets and more; JEI has the recipe). It places as one big machine, which has to stand on solid ground over the vein.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Run it.$() Put a drill head in, turn its rotation input at 30 RPM or more, and take the ore out of its IO block with a funnel or a chute. Faster rotation drills faster, and the head never wears out.$(br)$(li)$(bold)The Iron Drill head$() (Mining 50 to make) drills every vein in this pack. None of them needs the diamond or netherite head.

$(li)$(bold)Water veins$() take the Fluid Well Extractor instead: endless water for your pipes.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Hold W$() over the machine, the finder or the sample drill for its Ponder lesson.$(br)$(li)$(bold)Hardness still counts.$() Raw ore from a vein is gated like ore you dig. Below the Mining level its tier needs, you can carry it and keep it in a chest, but recipes, machines and other containers won't take it from you. Funnels, chutes and belts still move it. See $(l:lemursaucepacket:enchanting)Enchanting$(/l).

pages.title: Tool helpers
pages.text: $(#b9a98a)Tool - What it does$()$(br)$(bold)Excavator's Pickaxe (Mining 40)$() - Mines a 3 by 3: a wall in front of you, or a floor or ceiling when you look steeply up or down (more than 60°). Sneak to mine a single block. It only takes blocks a pickaxe mines.$(br)$(bold)Prospector's Pickaxe (Mining 30)$() - Ores come out already smelted$(br)$(bold)Telekinesis$() - An enchantment: what you break drops straight into your inventory ($(l:lemursaucepacket:enchanting)Enchanting$(/l))

$(bold)Tool Swapper upgrade (Crafting 25)$() - In the backpack you wear: left-click a block or a mob with the wrong tool and it swaps the right one into your hand$(br)$(bold)A spare tool$() - When a tool breaks, a matching one from your inventory takes its place$(br)$(bold)Extendo Grip (Attack 40 to hold)$() - In your off-hand: 3 more blocks of reach, 5 with one in each hand. With a backtank on, it uses air instead of durability.$(br)$(bold)Nuggets of Experience$() - Crushing raw ore in Create often gives one. Right-click it for experience, for the enchanting table and the anvil.

pages.title: Mining by machine
pages.text: $(li)$(bold)Mechanical drill$() (Mining 15 to make). It breaks the block in front of it, faster the faster it turns. On a moving contraption (a piston, bearing, gantry, minecart or train) it mines whatever it runs into, and what it digs goes into the contraption's chests.

$(li)$(bold)Borehead Bearing$() (Mining 40, with its Rock Cutting Wheels): a tunnel bore. The wheels break blocks all around themselves and attach without glue. What they dig goes into a storage block on the bore, and the bore stops when that's full. It spins at a quarter of the speed you give it, and the more it cuts at once, the slower it goes: use more than one bearing.$(br)$(li)$(bold)How hard machines dig.$() Create's drills, saws and rollers, and deployers holding a pickaxe, break blocks up to Hardness II: gold and redstone yes, diamonds and obsidian no ($(l:lemursaucepacket:enchanting)Enchanting$(/l)).

$(li)$(bold)Whose levels.$() A drill or saw works at the levels of its operator: whoever placed it or last right-clicked it. On a contraption, it keeps the operator it had when the contraption was put together. A log past the operator's Woodcutting stays standing. See $(l:lemursaucepacket:good-to-know)Good to know$(/l).$(br)$(li)$(bold)XP for whoever is near.$() A drill pays its Mining to every player within 16 blocks of it. Build an $(l:lemursaucepacket:create-tips)XP Bank$(/l) by your drills to keep a share while you're away.
